sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and learned HCGP for respondent No.1.
Respondent No.2, who NC: 2024:KHC:51201 is served in the matter has remained unrepresented before this Court.

3. FIR in Crime No.41/2024 was registered by Mandya Women Police Station against Mahadevaswamy and others for the aforesaid offences on the basis of the first information dated 29.06.2024 received from the victim girl who is aged about 17 years.
The petitioners herein are arrayed as accused Nos.9 and 10 in the FIR.

Apprehending arrest in the said case, the petitioners had filed Crl.Misc.No.555/2024 before the Jurisdictional Sessions Court and the same was rejected as against the petitioners herein on 12.09.2024.
Therefore, they are before this Court 4.
Learned counsel for the petitioners having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition, prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the bail application.
Accordingly, prays to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: Material on record would go to show that the petitioners herein are husband and wife and they are arrayed as accused Nos.9 and 10 in the FIR.
Only allegation against them is that they had approached the father of the victim girl with a proposal of marriage of accused No.1 with the victim girl.
Father of the victim girl, who is arrayed as accused No.12 has been granted anticipatory by the jurisdictional Sessions Court.
Only allegation against the petitioners is that they had abetted to commit the crime.

7. Considering the nature of allegation as found in the FIR against the petitioners and since there are no other criminal antecedents against them, I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the petitioners for grant of anticipatory bail is required to be answered affirmatively.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER The Criminal Petition is allowed.

The respondent - Police or any other police in the State of Karnataka are directed to release the petitioners NC: 2024:KHC:51201 in the event of their arrest in Crime No.41/2024 registered by Mandya Women police station for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 342, 354, 448, 376(3), 376(2)(n), 504, 506, 143 and 149 of IPC, Sections 6 and 17 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Sections 9, 10 and 11 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage (Karnataka Amendment)
Act, 2016, subject to the following conditions:
i).

Apprehending arrest in the said case, the petitioners had filed Crl.Misc.No.555/2024 before the Jurisdictional Sessions Court and the same was rejected as against the petitioners herein on 12.09.2024.
Accordingly, prays to dismiss the petition.
Material on record would go to show that the petitioners herein are husband and wife and they are arrayed as accused Nos.9 and 10 in the FIR.
Only allegation against them is that they had approached the father of the victim girl with a proposal of marriage of accused No.1 with the victim girl.
Father of the victim girl, who is arrayed as accused No.12 has been granted anticipatory by the jurisdictional Sessions Court.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, the following:
ORDER The Criminal Petition is allowed.
The respondent - Police or any other police in the State of Karnataka are directed to release the petitioners NC: 2024:KHC:51201 in the event of their arrest in Crime No.41/2024 registered by Mandya Women police station for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 342, 354, 448, 376(3), 376(2)(n), 504, 506, 143 and 149 of IPC, Sections 6 and 17 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and Sections 9, 10 and 11 of the Prohibition of Child Marriage (Karnataka Amendment)
Act, 2016, subject to the following conditions:
i).

ii). Petitioners shall regularly appear before the Trial Court without fail unless exempted by the Trial Court for valid reasons.
